note: EZH2 inhibitors (members lirametostat, tazemetostat, zeprumetostat) added to enzalutamide or abiraterone in castration-resistant prostate cancer, built on CRPC cell-line/xenograft re-sensitisation and the Rb1/Trp53 lineage-plasticity mouse; tazemetostat's approval package supplies the toxicology side. Mevrometostat entries are out of class and kept only so verdict indices stay valid.
label: Prostate cancer (EZH2 inhibitors)

engagement.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
engagement.note: CRPC cells stay dependent on EZH2 methyltransferase activity; the model read-out is H3K27me3 loss in tumour and blood cells. Opens the lirametostat track.
engagement.short: CRPC cells need EZH2 methyltransferase activity
engagement.quote: We found that the oncogenic function of EZH2 in cells of castration-resistant prostate cancer is independent of its role as a transcriptional repressor.
engagement.judgement: Opens the cell-line/xenograft track; Xiao 2018 (doi 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-18-0941) and Bai 2019 (doi 10.1074/jbc.RA119.008152) later showed EZH2 inhibition potentiates enzalutamide in CRPC cells and xenografts with H3K27me3 loss as the PD read-out.

engagement.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
engagement.note: Lirametostat 800 mg TID or 400 mg BID + cobicistat with enzalutamide or abiraterone lowered H3K27me3 in PBMCs and circulating tumour cells of mCRPC patients. Combination design (lirametostat added to enzalutamide or abiraterone): scored on the PD read-out.
engagement.short: H3K27me3 fell in patient PBMCs and CTCs
engagement.quote: Both CPI-1205 regimens resulted in significant target engagement (reduced H3K27me3 in PBMCs and CTCs).
engagement.confidence_note: AACR 2019 abstract (Cancer Research supplement); no magnitude given; sponsor cell-model data cited as Bradley 2018 are unpublished.
engagement.judgement: The abstract carries the preclinical claim (ARS-dependent prostate models sensitive to EZH2 inhibition, synergy with ARS inhibitors) beside the patient PD, so comparison_stated is true. The Tazverik FDA review (2020) adds dose-dependent skin H3K27me3 inhibition in the tazemetostat first-in-human study (EC50 734 ng·h/mL), other cancers.
engagement.magnitude_basis: H3K27me3 reduction in PBMCs/CTCs; no number reported

dose.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
dose.note: The prostate models stated no exposure target or tolerability margin; their implicit target is EZH2 inhibition sufficient to deplete tumour H3K27me3.
dose.short: No exposure target stated by the models
dose.quote: Hence, targeting the non-PRC2 function of EZH2 may have therapeutic efficacy for treating metastatic, hormone-refractory prostate cancer.
dose.judgement: Ku 2017 dosed inhibitors 'at concentrations sufficient to inhibit histone H3K27 methylation' and gave no PK target; the sponsors' lymphoma xenograft exposure targets (Kung 2018 for PF-06821497) are cross-indication and not used here.

efficacy.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
efficacy.note: CRPC cells depend on EZH2 as an AR coactivator; later work showed EZH2 inhibition re-sensitises enzalutamide-resistant cells and xenografts to AR blockade. Opens the tazemetostat track (EPZ6438 was dosed in the prostate models).
efficacy.short: EZH2 inhibition re-sensitises CRPC to AR blockade
efficacy.quote: We found that the oncogenic function of EZH2 in cells of castration-resistant prostate cancer is independent of its role as a transcriptional repressor.
efficacy.judgement: Class-level prediction: EZH2 inhibitor + AR pathway inhibitor beats AR pathway inhibitor alone in CRPC. Xiao 2018 screened epigenetic inhibitors and found EZH2 inhibitors specifically potentiated enzalutamide; Bai 2019 showed GSK126 + enzalutamide synergy and xenograft re-sensitisation. Constellation's and Epizyme's own cell data are unpublished.

efficacy.note: Rb1/Trp53 loss drives neuroendocrine-like plasticity and antiandrogen resistance; EZH2 inhibitors (EPZ6438, GSK126) restored AR and enzalutamide sensitivity in these tumours.
efficacy.short: EZH2i reverses plasticity in Rb1/Trp53-null tumours
efficacy.quote: Clinically relevant Ezh2 inhibitors restore androgen receptor expression and sensitivity to antiandrogen therapy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via PMC: EPZ6438 (tazemetostat) and GSK126 in vitro, GSK503 in SCID transplants (P=0.037 vs enzalutamide alone).
efficacy.judgement: Separate track because it is a different system with a different, patient-level prediction: benefit in RB1/TP53-deficient, neuroendocrine-like, antiandrogen-resistant disease. No member-drug trial has selected or stratified on RB1/TP53 loss or NE phenotype; ProSTAR, CELLO-1 and the mevrometostat studies enrolled unselected mCRPC, and MEVPRO-1/2 are unselected. Schweizer 2024 reports activity 'with and without androgen receptor and/or TP53 mutations', which is not a test of the prediction.
efficacy.reason: No RB1/TP53-selected trial of a member

efficacy.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
efficacy.note: CELLO-1 randomized phase 2 (n=81): tazemetostat 1200 mg BID + enzalutamide missed its rPFS primary endpoint; Ipsen stopped prostate development. Combination design: tazemetostat plus enzalutamide vs enzalutamide alone, scored on its rPFS primary endpoint like any other trial.
efficacy.quote: The study was terminated early as Sponsor decided to discontinue the development of tazemetostat in metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer and the primary endpoint was not met for this study.
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record (posted 2026-03-10) gives median rPFS 22.1 (16.6-27.6) vs 11.1 (5.7-16.5) months, n=41/40, with no test statistic; the sponsor states the primary endpoint was not met. An ESMO 2024 interim (abstract 1603P, doi 10.1016/j.annonc.2024.08.1684) reportedly gave BICR rPFS 16.6 vs 13.8 months, not significant; its text could not be retrieved verbatim.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on the final primary-endpoint verdict (2026), not the 2024 interim, because the interim was not the primary analysis and could not be quoted. Direction favoured the combination, but the primary endpoint failed and the drug was abandoned, so this is contra, not partial. One drug's contra beats mevrometostat's same on the same track; MEVPRO-1 cannot reverse it under the rules. ProSTAR (lirametostat, registry 2025-10-29): composite response 31.4% vs 17.1%, n=35/35, CIs overlap, never declared positive, program dropped; recorded in patient_trials, no status change.
efficacy.reason: One drug missed rPFS; contra beats same

patient_trials.quote: Efficacy: Composite Response Rate (%) for Phase 2 Randomized and Phase 2 Single-arm Treatment Groups

efficacy.model: Neuroendocrine CRPC patient-derived organoids and organoid xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor)
efficacy.note: Organoids from four CRPC-NE biopsies: EZH2 inhibitors GSK343/GSK503 had AR-independent single-agent activity at high doses, no synergy with enzalutamide; no NE-selected member trial. Only tool inhibitors (GSK343/GSK503) were run, so the track is tied to the class.
efficacy.short: EZH2i active in CRPC-NE organoids, untested
efficacy.quote: These data suggest that EZH2 inhibition has activity in CRPC-NE and this does not require expression of the AR.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC6008438, Nat Commun 9:2404, online 2018-06-19). Tool inhibitors GSK343 and GSK503, not a member drug; organoids OWCM154/OWCM155 vs adenocarcinoma MSK-PCa3; the matched PDOX kept EZH2/H3K27me3 but no in-vivo dosing is reported.
efficacy.judgement: Separate ex_vivo, patient-level track: patient-derived CRPC-NE organoids predict AR-independent single-agent benefit in neuroendocrine CRPC with no gain from adding enzalutamide, a different system and a different prediction from the Rb1/Trp53 GEMM (restored AR sensitivity). No member trial has enrolled or stratified NE/small-cell disease: ProSTAR (NCT03480646) and CELLO-1 (NCT04179864) were unselected mCRPC; zeprumetostat's NCT03741712 terminated 2019-09-30 at n=9 with no results; NCT04846478 (tazemetostat + talazoparib) is unselected with no results; the 2025-26 Hengrui trials NCT07230106 and NCT07407283 exclude neuroendocrine or small-cell histology. The comparison was never made.
efficacy.reason: No NE-selected trial of any member

efficacy.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
efficacy.note: Opens the lirametostat track on the CRPC cell-line/xenograft system (lirametostat's own cell data, Bradley 2018, are unpublished).
efficacy.quote: We found that the oncogenic function of EZH2 in cells of castration-resistant prostate cancer is independent of its role as a transcriptional repressor.
efficacy.judgement: Class-level prediction: EZH2 inhibitor + AR pathway inhibitor beats AR pathway inhibitor alone in CRPC. Xiao 2018 screened epigenetic inhibitors and found EZH2 inhibitors specifically potentiated enzalutamide; Bai 2019 showed GSK126 + enzalutamide synergy and xenograft re-sensitisation. Constellation's and Epizyme's own cell data are unpublished.

efficacy.model: Human CRPC cell lines and xenografts (EZH2 inhibitor + AR blockade)
efficacy.note: ProSTAR single-arm phase 2: lirametostat 800 mg TID + abiraterone/prednisone composite response 21.4% (6/28); ORR 0%, PSA50 2/28. Single-arm design with no stated success bar, scored on direction. Randomized arm (31.4% vs 17.1%, no test) unresolved.
efficacy.quote: Efficacy: Composite Response Rate (%) for Phase 2 Randomized and Phase 2 Single-arm Treatment Groups
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record (posted 2025-10-29), tables only; the quote is the outcome title. No pre-specified success bar is posted; composite response = CTC30 conversion or objective response, n=28 evaluable.
efficacy.judgement: Single-arm ruling: a response where the model predicted one is same. The randomized enzalutamide comparison favours the combination but posts no test, so it does not settle anything on its own; ORR 0% and the program's 2020 discontinuation keep this partial and low confidence.
efficacy.reason: Single-arm composite response, randomized arm unresolved
efficacy.magnitude_basis: composite response rate 21.4% (95% CI 8.3-41.0) in the single arm

safety.note: Tazemetostat rat/monkey studies flagged GI mucosa, bone marrow, lymphoid depletion and bone; rats later developed T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma.
safety.short: Rat tox: GI, marrow, lymphoid, bone
safety.quote: Target organs included stomach (erosion/ulceration and mucosal hyperplasia), jejunum (crypt hyperplasia), ileum, kidney, bone marrow, lymphoid tissues (lymphoid depletion), and bone (osteoblast hyperplasia and new trabecular bone formation).
safety.confidence_note: Opener year is a proxy: the review does not date the 4-week rat study (K12004); tazemetostat's first-in-human study began 2013.
safety.judgement: Toxicology from the only approved member stands in for the class; lirametostat and mevrometostat packages are unpublished.

safety.note: Rat T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma predicted secondary haematologic malignancy; 6 of 822 pooled tazemetostat patients developed MDS, AML or T-LBL. Imported: no prostate patient had tazemetostat safety data public in 2020.
safety.short: Rat T-LBL matched clinical secondary malignancies
safety.quote: As T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma occurred in juvenile and adult rats during 13-week toxicity studies and EZH2 loss-of-function mutations have been identified in patients with spontaneous hematologic malignancies, the development of secondary malignancies may be an on-target effect of tazemetostat.
safety.confidence_note: Pooled safety population of 822 solid-tumour and haematologic patients, not prostate; epithelioid sarcoma NDA.
safety.judgement: Regulator states the rat-to-patient comparison. Rat T-LBL arose at >=2.8x the 800 mg BID human AUC (label 8.4), so the margin was misplaced in exposure terms, but the harm itself was predicted: same, direction only. Imported from the epithelioid sarcoma package.
safety.magnitude_basis: secondary haematologic malignancy, 6/822 (0.7%) vs rat T-LBL at >=2.8x human AUC

safety.note: CELLO-1 mCRPC patients on tazemetostat + abiraterone or enzalutamide showed the known GI and marrow profile, no new signal; imported-harm ruling: prostate patients were measured, so they set the status.
safety.short: Prostate patients: known GI/marrow profile only
safety.quote: The safety profile and clinical activity of TAZ + A/P and of TAZ + E were maintained and were consistent with the prior analysis of the phase 1b data. No new safety signals were identified.
safety.confidence_note: SUO 2022 congress abstract (no DOI found); grade 3/4 TEAEs 47.6% of 21. Registry NCT04179864 results (posted 2026-03-10): phase 2 diarrhoea 15/41 vs 8/40, anaemia 9/41 vs 3/40, no MDS, AML or lymphoma among 63 tazemetostat-treated men.
safety.judgement: Imported-harm ruling: prostate patients were measured, so their result replaces the follicular-lymphoma SYMPHONY-1 import. The rat GI and bone-marrow target organs held; the rat T-LBL / secondary haematologic malignancy was not seen in prostate trials too small and short to show it, hence partial. Previously: Tazemetostat withdrawn worldwide after SYMPHONY-1 showed haematologic second primary malignancies in 5.7% vs none; authors call it on-target EZH2 biology relevant to prostate phase 3.
safety.reason: Prostate patients showed the predicted GI/marrow harms
safety.magnitude_basis: GI and haematologic TEAE incidence vs rat target organs; haematologic SPM 0/63
